2. library SportsAnalytics270 has a function final_table. It creates final league standing for the season. Use this function to create a dataframe with final standings of all seasons of your league. Combine seasons into 1 datafrmae. You need to get something like nba_east. You can use for loop here.

2.1 Create a variable with a winning percentage. Note, as there are draws in football, we are going to take draw as a half win (use a for loop here). (2p)

```{r}
data("f_data_sm")
dd <- f_data_sm %>% filter(COUNTRY=="Italy") 

seriea <-c()
season <- unique(dd$SEASON)
for (j in season){
  s1 <- final_table(dd, season = j, country = "Italy")
  s1$season <- j
  seriea <-rbind(seriea,s1)
}

seriea$Wpct <- (seriea$W+seriea$D*0.5)/seriea$M
```


3. Plot Goal differential agains Winning Percentage.
3.1 Add regression line and make your plot pretty. Do you see relationship ? (3p)

```{r}
ggplot(seriea, aes(x=DIFF, y=Wpct))+geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method='lm') + 
  labs(x="Goal Difference", y = "Winning percentage", 
       title="Winning % and goal differential")
```


3.2 Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient for Goal differential and Winning Percentage. What you think ? (1p)

```{r}
cor(seriea$DIFF, seriea$Wpct)
```


4. Your goal is to build a regression model to estimate the k value from Pythagorean formula. Show all the steps, interpret results. (4p)

```{r}
seriea$Ratio <- seriea$GF/seriea$GA
seriea <- seriea[seriea$L !=0,]
seriea$W1 <- seriea$W+0.5*seriea$D
seriea$L1 <- seriea$L+0.5*seriea$D
model <- lm(log(W1/L1)~0+log(Ratio), data=seriea)
summary(model)
```


5. Using estimated k value, calculate Pythagorean Winning percentage and Pythagorean wins for each team. (1p)

```{r}
seriea$PW_perc <- seriea$GF^1.26829/(seriea$GF^1.26829+seriea$GA^1.26829)
seriea$PW <- round(seriea$PW_perc*seriea$M)
```


6. Now find overperforming and underperforming teams. (1p)


```{r}
# If the difference is positive then we have overperforming teams,
# if negative we have underperforming teams
seriea$PW_df <- (seriea$W+seriea$D*0.5 -  seriea$PW) 

seriea %>% filter(season ==2018) %>%
  select(TEAM, PW_df) %>%
  arrange(desc(PW_df))
```


### Elo

Your goal is to build Elo rating model for NBA games. The data can be found - 
```{r}
library(SportsAnalytics270)
data("nba2009_2021")
```

In your model be sure that: You have adjusted elo ratings at the begining of each season. (5p) 

Please follow the link for info here - https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/how-we-calculate-nba-elo-ratings/ .
you need to use for loop here, if you have a trouble with it , let me know.

```{r}
nn <- c()
df<-c()
w <- rep(1500, 30)
names(w)<-unique(nba2009_2021$home.TEAM_NAME)
season<-unique(nba2009_2021$SEASON_ID)
# Loop to recalculate rating after each season
for (i in season) {
    nn <- elo.run(score(home.PTS, away.PTS) ~ adjust(home.TEAM_NAME, 100) +
              away.TEAM_NAME, data = nba2009_2021[nba2009_2021$SEASON_ID == i,], k = 20, initial.elos = w)
    w <- elo::final.elos(nn)
    # Adjust the rating
    w<-w*0.75+0.25*1505
    nn <- as.data.frame(nn)
    nn <- data.frame(nn, season = i)
    df<-rbind(df, nn)
}

# Take out Boston Celtics game
df <- df[df$wins.A !=0.5,]
```


Try different values for home team advantage, K, anything else ?. (5p)

